abstract: Maintains ambient cleanroom acoustic and chemical background noise floor records
system_message:
You are the Ambient baseline monitoring lead (MON). Your responsibility is to maintain ambient cleanroom acoustic and chemical background noise floor records, alongside ambient relative humidity tolerances for cleanroom contamination localization protocols under evaluation in the advanced photolithography bay.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains ambient cleanroom acoustic and chemical background noise floor records（BASE）
information_points.content:
MON-BASE-D14：For Proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight spectrometry, the background noise floor across the photolithography track enclosure under sealed laminar flow is 30 ppb, determined as a three-sigma baseline fluctuation concentration equivalent using an aggregation window of a trailing 24-hour average.
MON-BASE-NWD：For the Cavity ring-down spectroscopic point grid, the background noise floor across the photolithography track enclosure under sealed laminar flow is 45 ppb, measured as a three-sigma baseline fluctuation concentration equivalent using an aggregation window of a trailing 24-hour average.
MON-BASE-Y3T：For Differential vacuum photoionization mass spectrometry, the background noise floor across the photolithography track enclosure under sealed laminar flow is 45 ppb, determined as a three-sigma baseline fluctuation concentration equivalent using an aggregation window of a trailing 30-day average.
MON-BASE-8DZ：For Differential vacuum photoionization mass spectrometry, the background noise floor across the photolithography track enclosure under sealed laminar flow is 10 ppb, evaluated as a three-sigma baseline fluctuation concentration equivalent using an aggregation window of a trailing 24-hour average.

information_points.title: Relative humidity tolerance（HUMID）
information_points.content:
MON-HUMID-TVE：The Cavity ring-down spectroscopic point grid specifies a maximum permissible relative humidity of 50% across the track and scanner cleanroom envelope.
MON-HUMID-IYD：Proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight spectrometry specifies a maximum permissible relative humidity of 40% across the track and scanner cleanroom envelope.
MON-HUMID-9QI：Differential vacuum photoionization mass spectrometry specifies a maximum permissible relative humidity of 45% within the track and scanner cleanroom envelope to prevent optical condensation.
